nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Query/path/explain return a scoped subgraph much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; graphify update after code changes is AST-only with no API cost.

nodes.label: National Address Database (NAD)
nodes.rationale: US Public Domain government source; primary reference dataset for the verification stack.

nodes.label: OpenAddresses (OA)
nodes.rationale: Community/open-data source, not government; fetched via Batch API with per-source config in .data/midwest_sources.json.

nodes.label: OpenStreetMap (OSM)
nodes.rationale: ODbL-licensed; Geofabrik PBF mirrors, one per state.

nodes.label: State/County ArcGIS Open-Data Portals (not yet integrated)
nodes.norm_label: state/county arcgis open-data portals (not yet integrated)

nodes.label: Melissa Global Address Cloud API (doGlobalAddress)
nodes.rationale: One request carries up to ~100 records, the foundation of the batching strategy: one HTTP round-trip verifies an entire batch and many batches run concurrently.

nodes.label: MelissaConfig
nodes.rationale: All tunables come from environment variables so the same image behaves correctly in every environment; fails fast at startup if the license key is absent.

nodes.label: MelissaAddressClient
nodes.rationale: Translates HTTP status into transient (429/5xx) vs terminal (other 4xx) exception types so the resilience pipeline retries only what is safe to retry.

nodes.label: BatchAddressVerifier
nodes.rationale: Bounded SemaphoreSlim caps in-flight requests to the Melissa contract concurrency limit (back-pressure); failed batches are replaced with SE01 error sentinels so one bad batch never aborts the run; results re-aligned by RecordID for deterministic order.

nodes.label: ResiliencePolicies (Polly v8 Pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Ordered retry -> circuit breaker -> rate limiter -> per-attempt timeout; contract limits, not raw machine capacity, are the binding throughput constraint, which is why the app rate-limits itself.

nodes.label: ResultInterpreter
nodes.rationale: Downstream systems should branch on a single verdict enum, not raw codes scattered through the pipeline; parses the comma-delimited Results string once.

nodes.label: VerificationWorker
nodes.rationale: Batch-mode hosted service: runs the batch then calls StopApplication so the container exits cleanly when the run completes.

nodes.label: Melissa Result Codes (AV/AC/AE/GS families)
nodes.rationale: AV2x = full verification (final digit = granularity), AV1x = partial only, AC = corrections, AE = errors, GS/GE = geocode status; the Results string is the authoritative signal for downstream logic.

nodes.label: Terraform Azure Container Apps Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Two-pass apply because the container app references an image in a registry created by the same configuration; .NET/Docker layers are cloud-agnostic so only the Terraform layer changes per platform.

nodes.label: KEDA Queue-Depth Scaling
nodes.rationale: Two independent scaling axes: vertical (async concurrency inside a replica) and horizontal (KEDA replicas on queue depth, scale-to-zero); the product of per-replica concurrency and replica count must still respect the Melissa contract.

nodes.label: Key Vault License-Key Secret Management
nodes.rationale: License key never baked into source or image; injected via managed identity from Key Vault; body-based auth keeps the key out of URLs and logs.

nodes.label: Address Verification Stack (NAD)
nodes.rationale: Browser -> nginx -> C# API -> PostgreSQL; user picks one of the three closest fuzzy matches which is then saved to nad_sub.

nodes.label: nad PostgreSQL Database (il_addresses)
nodes.rationale: Reused, not recreated, by Terraform: the container already holds ~4.86M Illinois addresses so destroying it would throw the data away; managed by tools/start_postgres.py, reached via host.docker.internal:5433.

nodes.label: pg_trgm Trigram Similarity Search
nodes.rationale: Index (db/01_init_nad.sql) and query (api/AddressRepository.cs) deliberately share the same normalized concatenated expression; GIN gin_trgm_ops lets % find candidates quickly, then similarity() ranks and the top 3 are returned.

nodes.label: C# API Endpoints (/api/health, /api/verify, /api/submit, /api/stats)
nodes.rationale: NAD_TABLE env var selects the searched table (il_addresses default); pointing at the national nad_addresses table requires setting nad_table in terraform/variables.tf and adding a trigram index.

nodes.label: start.py Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Ensures Docker + Postgres, initializes pg_trgm and the one-time trigram index (minutes on ~5M rows, cached in the volume), then terraform init/apply for API and web containers; --down keeps PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Terraform (kreuzwerker/docker) Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Owns only the API and web containers and their network; PostgreSQL is deliberately outside Terraform to protect loaded data.

nodes.label: Phase 0 - Baseline Measurement
nodes.rationale: No code changes; numbers are the yardstick for every later phase. Spec 05 interference is expected to fail - that is the bug, not the test.

nodes.label: Phase 1 - Npgsql Pool & Prepare Tuning
nodes.rationale: Pool settings applied in code via NpgsqlConnectionStringBuilder so they hold regardless of env-var contents; Multiplexing=true deliberately deferred to Phase 7 because it changes failure semantics and deserves its own A/B; Postgres max_connections must exceed 2x MaxPoolSize.

nodes.label: Phase 2 - Stats Cache + Parallelize
nodes.rationale: 30s TTL plus single-flight guard so a stampede of cold-cache callers cannot launch N aggregate scans; both databases queried concurrently with Task.WhenAll; worst rollback case is stale-by-30s stats which the UI tolerates.

nodes.label: Phase 3 - Cancellation Propagation
nodes.rationale: Minimal APIs bind CancellationToken from HttpContext.RequestAborted; Npgsql translates token cancellation into a Postgres CANCEL so abandoned queries stop consuming DB CPU.

nodes.label: Phase 4 - nginx Upstream Keepalive
nodes.rationale: upstream block with keepalive 256 + proxy_http_version 1.1 + empty Connection header; verified by through-proxy RPS within a few percent of direct and flat TIME-WAIT count.

nodes.label: Phase 5 - Verify-Result Cache (10K enabler)
nodes.rationale: NAD reference data is read-only between bulk reloads so identical queries always produce identical results; key is the normalized lowercased whitespace-collapsed query; negative caching with shorter TTL for empty results; invalidation is implicit via app restart on reload; hit/miss counters exposed on /api/health. The one phase that changes the capacity class of the system.

nodes.label: Phase 6 - JSON Source-Gen + Micro-Optimizations
nodes.rationale: Source-generated JsonSerializerContext, typed NpgsqlParameter, GetFloat instead of boxing Convert.ToDouble, dev-only CORS; verify response bodies byte-identical because field casing can silently change when switching resolvers.

nodes.label: Phase 7 - Scale-Out (conditional)
nodes.rationale: Decision gate: proceed only if miss volume x per-miss DB cost exceeds ~60% of one Postgres box after the Phase 5 cache soaks; covers Multiplexing A/B, horizontal API instances (stateless + per-instance cache, no coordination), and read replicas with writes pinned to primary.

nodes.label: 10K req/s Capacity Math
nodes.rationale: 10,000 req/s x ~20ms Postgres CPU per trigram search = ~200 CPU-seconds/second, i.e. ~200 Postgres cores of pure search work; no C# change fixes that - only caching and read replicas do.

nodes.label: Finding 1 - Npgsql Pool Defaults Collapse Under Load
nodes.rationale: Default Maximum Pool Size 100 is exactly the Little's-law minimum at 10K req/s and 10ms/query, so any latency spike exhausts the pool; no Max Auto Prepare means every query is re-planned; 30s default timeouts stack deep queues instead of failing fast.
nodes.norm_label: finding 1 - npgsql pool defaults collapse under load

nodes.label: Finding 2 - ZIP Fast Path Computes similarity() For Every Row
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY score DESC cannot use any index so similarity is evaluated for all rows in the ZIP; the in-code comment about LIMIT-survivor evaluation is true only for the KNN path; a 5-digit number matching no zip_code costs two full round trips.
nodes.norm_label: finding 2 - zip fast path computes similarity() for every row

nodes.label: Finding 3 - No Cancellation Propagation
nodes.rationale: Without CancellationToken, client disconnects leave Postgres burning CPU on work nobody will read; under overload with retries this is an amplification loop: dead queries slow the DB, causing more timeouts, causing more retries.

nodes.label: Finding 4 - /api/stats Is a Denial-of-Service Button
nodes.rationale: Every call runs count(*) over 4.86M rows plus two GROUP BYs on both databases sequentially with no caching; a handful of stats requests per second starves all verify traffic.

nodes.label: Finding 5 - nginx Opens a New TCP Connection Per Request
nodes.rationale: proxy_pass defaults to HTTP/1.0 with Connection: close; at 10K req/s that is 10K TCP handshakes per second and eventual ephemeral-port exhaustion on the proxy.
nodes.norm_label: finding 5 - nginx opens a new tcp connection per request

nodes.label: Finding 6 - Smaller Free Wins
nodes.rationale: JSON source-gen, GetFloat over boxing Convert.ToDouble, typed NpgsqlParameter, dev-gated CORS, ThreadPool.SetMinThreads; none move the needle like findings 1-2 but each is a one-line change.

nodes.label: Verify-Result Cache Lever
nodes.rationale: NAD is read-only reference data so identical queries always return identical results; an in-memory LRU or Redis keyed on the normalized query absorbs most real-world traffic because address lookups repeat heavily. The only path to 10K req/s on realistic hardware.

nodes.label: Postgres Read Replicas (NpgsqlMultiHostDataSource)
nodes.rationale: Handles the cache-miss remainder; NpgsqlMultiHostDataSource load-balances across standbys with no application-code changes beyond the connection string; writes stay pinned to the primary.

nodes.label: Playwright Performance Test Suite
nodes.rationale: For latency SLOs, regression detection, and finding the single-instance saturation knee - not for generating 10K req/s; hits the API container directly at localhost:8081 by default; PERF_SEED makes the workload mix reproducible.

nodes.label: Spec 02 - Verify Latency Per Code Path
nodes.rationale: Measures ZIP fast path, full trigram KNN, and the bad-ZIP double-query fallthrough; these numbers drive all capacity math.
nodes.norm_label: spec 02 - verify latency per code path

nodes.label: Spec 03 - Closed-Loop Throughput Ramp
nodes.rationale: Finds the knee of the curve and extrapolates instances needed for the 10K req/s target.

nodes.label: Spec 04 - Submit Write-Path Performance
nodes.rationale: Writes real rows tagged PERFTEST:: into nad_sub.submissions so they can be deleted after the run.

nodes.label: Spec 05 - Stats Cost & Interference
nodes.rationale: Measures the uncached full-table aggregates and whether stats traffic degrades verify latency; fails by design until stats is cached - it encodes the stats-DoS finding empirically.

nodes.label: Spec 06 - Mixed Open-Loop Soak (90/8/2)
nodes.rationale: Constant-arrival-rate soak; saturation shows up as shed requests, not silently lower throughput.

nodes.label: k6 Open-Loop 10K Test (k6/verify-10k.js)
nodes.rationale: A single Node/Playwright process tops out around 1-2K req/s even against a no-op endpoint, so the literal 10K test needs a purpose-built open-loop generator run from machines that are not the machine under test.

nodes.label: Capacity Math Note (perf README)
nodes.rationale: The database is the real constraint, not Kestrel: ~20ms Postgres CPU per trigram search means ~200 Postgres cores at 10K req/s unless most requests are served from a cache.
